answer: One concrete defense is a staked identity bond: every agent must lock collateral to enter the shared lagoon of participants, and any cheating is slashed after peer attestation. A sybil attacker cannot cheaply echo a single bond across a thousand fake identities, because each new address demands its own fresh locked stake. If a node like juniper spins up clones, each clone needs new collateral, so the attack cost scales linearly with the identity count while an honest agent pays once and later recovers its bond.
